g1.label: 1. Where and when was Naledi born?
g1.why: The opening sentence says Naledi was born in 1955 in Soweto, a township outside Johannesburg.

g2.label: 2. Why couldn’t Naledi train as a nurse?
g2.why: Paragraph two says her school stayed closed after the uprising and she had to leave; paragraph three says that without her certificate she could not get a place at a nursing college.

accept: She carried a wounded boy to safety
g3.label: 3. What did Naledi do during the 1976 uprising?
g3.why: Paragraph two says Naledi, standing near the front, carried a wounded boy to safety.

g4.correct: She would have waited six days if necessary
accept: She would have waited six days if necessary
g4.label: 4. What does Naledi say about the queue at the 1994 election?
g4.why: She says she stood in the queue for six hours, but she would have waited six days.

g5.correct: It describes an action completed before another past event
accept: It describes an action completed before another past event
g5.label: 5. In “the government had decided that Black children should be prepared mainly for manual work”, why is had decided in the past perfect?
g5.why: The past perfect marks an action completed before another past event: the government's decision came before Naledi's wish to become a nurse.

g6.label: 6. (Review) In "Black families were forced to live separately", what voice is it?
g6.why: Review from 10g-scottish-history: the subject receives the action — were + past participle is passive.

g1.label: 1. By the time Mandela left prison, he ___ 27 years behind bars.
g1.why: By the time marks the later past event — the earlier action takes the past perfect.

g2.label: 2. Naledi ___ for the first time in 1994.
g2.why: A completed single event in the past takes the simple past.

g3.label: 3. While she ___ in the queue, she thought of her father.
g3.why: An ongoing background action takes the past continuous: was standing.

g4.label: 4. The apartheid government ___ to power in 1948.
g4.why: A dated event in the past (1948) takes the simple past.

g5.label: 5. Most Black South Africans ___ never voted before 1994.
g5.why: Before 1994 looks back from a past point — the past perfect: had never voted.

g6.label: 6. From 1962 to 1968, she ___ primary school in Soweto.
g6.why: A finished period in the past with no later past event to look back from takes the simple past: attended.

g7.label: 7. When the radio ___ the results, people ran into the streets.
g7.why: Two past events in sequence take the simple past: announced, ran.

g8.label: 8. By 1994, Naledi ___ to vote for almost twenty years.
g8.why: By 1994 is a point in the past, and the wanting lasted up to it, so it takes the past perfect: had wanted.

g1.label: 1. ___ Mandela became president, he had spent 27 years in prison.
g1.why: The main clause is past perfect, so the conjunction must mark the later event: before.

g2.label: 2. By the time Naledi voted, she ___ for almost forty years.
g2.why: By the time + past takes the past perfect: the waiting was complete by then.

g3.label: 3. It was the first time she ___ in a national election.
g3.why: After "it was the first time", English uses the past perfect: had voted.

g4.label: 4. ___ the flag rose over Pretoria, the crowd fell silent.
g4.why: Two simultaneous past actions are linked with as, meaning while.

g5.label: 5. ___ the celebrations began, it started to rain.
g5.why: Just as marks two events happening at exactly the same moment.

g6.label: 6. Naledi had lived in the same street ___ 1955.
g6.why: A starting point in time takes since; for is used with a duration.

g7.label: 7. Two years ___ the election, South Africa had a new constitution.
g7.why: Two years after the election counts forward from a past event (1994 to 1996). Ago counts back from today, and before would mean 1992.

g8.label: 8. She had never ___ hope before that day.
g8.why: Had never + past participle — the past perfect needs felt, not the base form.
